item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00220","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C15","C06","C10"],"selected_candidate_label":"C15","confidence":0.86,"relationship_type":"structural_functional_template","rationale":"C15 plausibly supplied a material argumentative template for the child: both letters contend that raising or restoring agricultural price-support incentives would increase government-held surpluses and thereby undermine the intended benefits of current farm policy. The child adapts C15's dairy-support argument to defend the soil bank proposal. C06 shares the agricultural-surplus setting but focuses on distributing perishables, while C10 offers only a more general principle that one economic policy should not nullify another.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"these price-depressing surpluses themselves are largely the result of high rigid price supports of wartime, too long continued in time of peace","parent_excerpt":"an increase in this [dairy support] level would be injurious, not helpful, to the dairy industry, for it would diminish the consumption of dairy products, increase the accumulation of surplus stocks","explanation":"Both identify elevated price supports as a cause of harmful agricultural-surplus accumulation."},{"child_excerpt":"It would be inconsistent to enact a soil bank program and, at the same time, reestablish production incentives that would again fill government warehouses, again depress prices, and thus defeat the main object of the soil bank.","parent_excerpt":"Because both of these provisions are clearly at variance with the objectives being sought, I hope they can be withdrawn in your conference deliberations.","explanation":"Both oppose farm-bill provisions on the ground that they conflict with and would frustrate the program's own objectives."},{"child_excerpt":"I should be gravely concerned if the soil bank should be coupled with the restitution of production incentives certain to nullify the great benefits that the bank can bring.","parent_excerpt":"To me, it is inescapable that an increase in this level would be injurious, not helpful","explanation":"The child reuses the same functional structure: acknowledge a proposed farm-policy modification, predict counterproductive production or surplus effects, and urge against coupling it with the beneficial program."}]}
